key_cases.holding: The division held that a county department may not seek involuntary termination through an article 5 relinquishment proceeding while an article 3 dependency and neglect case is open, because the dependency court retains continuing exclusive jurisdiction over the child's status until majority or until that jurisdiction is otherwise terminated.
key_cases.relevance: This is the clearest published Colorado statement of how long the dependency court's jurisdiction over an adjudicated child runs, which is the framework for continued placement as a youth approaches majority.
key_cases.quote: the dependency and neglect court maintains continuing, exclusive jurisdiction over any child who has been adjudicated dependent and neglected.

key_cases.holding: The court held that section 19-1-109(1) authorizes an appeal from any final order in a dependency or neglect proceeding, that subsection (2) adds to rather than limits that right, and that C.A.R. 3.4(a) cannot narrow the categories of orders the statute makes appealable.
key_cases.relevance: Because the statute governs appeals from any final order, it is the vehicle for challenging orders about a youth's continued placement and the court's continuing jurisdiction.
key_cases.quote: we hold that section 19-1-109(1) authorizes the appeal of any order from a dependency or neglect proceeding that is "final"

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed in part and reversed in part, holding that UCCJEA temporary emergency jurisdiction is limited to abandoned children and to emergencies of mistreatment or abuse, that the juvenile court therefore lacked that jurisdiction when it terminated parental rights and the termination judgment was properly vacated, but that the division erred in directing contact with an Arkansas court without first analysing whether Arkansas had home-state jurisdiction on the date of the termination order.
key_cases.relevance: Continuing authority over a youth's placement depends on a UCCJEA jurisdictional basis that exists at the time each order is entered, not merely at the time the case was opened.
key_cases.quote: we hold that UCCJEA temporary emergency jurisdiction exists only to protect abandoned children or to prevent mistreatment or abuse in emergencies
